verses.context: Comparing the promised land's rest to something still available under a new covenant, the writer declares that a Sabbath rest remains for God's people.

KJV.text: Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope.
KJV.displayText: Therefore my heart is glad, and my glory rejoiceth: my flesh also shall rest in hope.

BSB.text: Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices; my body also will dwell securely.
BSB.displayText: Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices; my body also will dwell securely.

CPDV.text: Because of this, my heart has been joyful, and my tongue has exulted. Moreover, even my body will rest in hope.
CPDV.displayText: Because of this, my heart has been joyful, and my tongue has exulted. Moreover, even my body will rest in hope.

verses.context: Continuing that same reflection, David describes a settled gladness and hope, words later applied in the New Testament to Christ's resurrection.

KJV.text: Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.
KJV.displayText: Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.

BSB.text: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”
BSB.displayText: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”

CPDV.text: But certainly, he did not leave himself without testimony, doing good from heaven, giving rains and fruitful seasons, filling their hearts with food and gladness.”
CPDV.displayText: But certainly, he did not leave himself without testimony, doing good from heaven, giving rains and fruitful seasons, filling their hearts with food and gladness.”

verses.context: Speaking to a crowd in Lystra who want to worship him and Barnabas as gods, Paul insists God has always shown himself through good gifts like rain and harvest.
